keyTerms.definition: The record of which sources each lesson concept comes from.
Prerequisite modules: vectors, geometry, linear maps; spectral and numerical linear algebra.

recall.question: Does this lesson reproduce the instructor's lectures?
recall.answer: No. It is locally authored bridge content for prerequisites P03 and P04.

keyTerms.definition: The geometry of vectors and matrices that every ML method stands on.
A skill the learner can show after the lesson.

recall.question: What must a learner be able to do after this lesson?
recall.answer: Draw the geometry of any 2 by 2 matrix, compute each decomposition by hand on a toy, verify it in code, and name the numerical cost of every operation.

keyTerms.definition: 0-10 markers of the Russian-doll ladder position of each step.
Concrete question, toy, rule, computed example, code, checks, costs, alternatives, failure case.

recall.question: What do shell numbers mark?
recall.answer: The Russian-doll ladder position of each step, from 0 to 10.

keyTerms.definition: A flat world through the origin: closed under addition and stretching.
The set of all combinations of the given arrows.
The count of independent directions.
The count of independent directions of a matrix.

recall.question: When is a set of arrows a subspace?
recall.answer: When adding two arrows stays in the set and stretching any arrow stays in the set.

recall.question: Why is the unit disk not a subspace?
recall.answer: Doubling the arrow [0.7, 0] leaves the disk; the addition rule breaks.

keyTerms.definition: The count of directions that survive a matrix.
The set of arrows the matrix kills, landing on zero.
The world of all outputs of the matrix.

recall.question: For M = [[1,2],[2,4]], what are the rank and nullspace?
recall.answer: Rank 1, nullspace = span([-2, 1]), and 1 + 1 = 2, the input dimension.

recall.question: Why does [[1,0],[0,1e-9]] mislead threshold rank?
recall.answer: True rank 2 but behaves like rank 1 in float32. Use the sigma gap instead.

keyTerms.definition: Signed agreement: the sum of matching-item products.
The length of an arrow.
Dot product divided by the two lengths; the cosine of the angle.

recall.question: What are the dot product, norm, and cosine for v=[3,4], w=[1,0]?
recall.answer: Dot = 3, norm = 5, cos = 0.6, angle 53.13 degrees.

recall.question: Why normalize before comparing agreement?
recall.answer: [100,0] dot [-1,0] = -100: huge magnitude, negative agreement. Normalize across scales.

keyTerms.definition: The shadow of an arrow dropped straight down onto a line.
The leftover b minus proj, orthogonal to the line.
Projection: the best fit is the shadow of the target on the column space.

recall.question: What is the check for a projection, every time?
recall.answer: Orthogonality: the residual dotted with the line direction is zero.

recall.question: What breaks when projecting onto the zero arrow?
recall.answer: Division by zero. The formula has no answer.

keyTerms.definition: A recipe applied to every arrow: rotate, stretch, shear, or project.
Where the unit axes land; read them to see the transform.

recall.question: What does R = [[0,-1],[1,0]] do to [1,0]?
recall.answer: Rotates 90 degrees: R @ [1,0] = [0,1].

recall.question: How do you read a matrix as a transform?
recall.answer: Read the columns: the first is where [1,0] lands, the second where [0,1] lands.

keyTerms.definition: The signed area scale factor of a matrix.
Determinant zero: the matrix crushes area to zero.

recall.question: What is det([[2,1],[1,2]]) and what does it mean?
recall.answer: 3: the unit square maps to a parallelogram of area 3.

recall.question: Why is a tiny determinant not proof of near-singularity?
recall.answer: D scaled by 1e-6 has tiny determinant yet is perfectly invertible. Determinant measures volume, not invertibility quality.

keyTerms.definition: The undo: D^{-1} D = I.
The best possible undo: inverts kept directions, returns zero for killed ones.

recall.question: How do you solve D x = b correctly?
recall.answer: Use solve(D, b). Never form inv(D) @ b: slower and less accurate.

recall.question: What does the pseudoinverse give for singular Z?
recall.answer: The shortest arrow x with Z x closest to b.

keyTerms.definition: A direction a matrix leaves alone: E v = lambda v.
The stretch factor along the eigenvector.

recall.question: What are the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of [[2,1],[1,2]]?
recall.answer: [1,1] with stretch 3, [1,-1] with stretch 1. The two are perpendicular.

recall.question: Which matrix has no real eigenvectors?
recall.answer: Rotation by 90 degrees: it turns every arrow, so no real direction survives.

keyTerms.definition: M = U Sigma V^T: rotate, stretch by singular values, rotate.
The true stretch factors: sigma = [5, 3] for the toy.

recall.question: What is the rank-1 reconstruction error for sigma = [5,3]?
recall.answer: 3.0, exactly sigma_2. The dropped value names the price.

recall.question: Why never form M^T M to get singular values?
recall.answer: It squares the conditioning. Use the SVD directly on ill-conditioned M.

keyTerms.definition: Positive semidefinite: x^T A x never goes negative.
All eigenvalues >= 0. The test to use.

recall.question: Is [[1,2],[2,1]] PSD?
recall.answer: No: at x = [1,-1] the value is -2.0, and the eigenvalues are 3 and -1.

recall.question: Why not test min_eig > 0 strictly on floats?
recall.answer: Rounding can show -1e-16 for a truly PSD matrix. Use min_eig >= -tol.

keyTerms.definition: The average product of deviations from the mean.
Covariance divided by the two standard deviations, in [-1, 1].

recall.question: What does the off-diagonal 2.3333 say?
recall.answer: x and y rise together. Correlation 0.9899: the two features are nearly locked.

recall.question: Does zero covariance mean independence?
recall.answer: No. Points on a circle have covariance ~0 but are perfectly related.

keyTerms.definition: kappa = sigma_max / sigma_min: the error amplifier.
Relative output error <= kappa times relative input error.

recall.question: What did the K toy measure?
recall.answer: A 3.54e-07 input nudge became a 7.07e-04 answer move: about 2000x, under kappa = 4002.

recall.question: What does kappa = 4002 leave in float32?
recall.answer: About 3 good digits. In float16 the same problem can return pure noise.

keyTerms.definition: Intuition, equation, code, observation for every matrix claim.
The survivors: directions the matrix keeps.

recall.question: What are the four ways?
recall.answer: Intuition: matrices stretch and rotate space. Equation: M = U Sigma V^T. Code: svd, solve, eigvalsh. Observation: measured numbers obey the bounds.
